intro: A derivative measures local change. Evaluating a function just before and after a point gives an independent way to check an analytic gradient.
task: Return the central-difference estimate of the derivative of scalar function f at x using step h.
requirements: Require a callable f, finite scalar x, and positive finite scalar h. Reject invalid inputs with ValueError.
Reject steps that round x+h or x-h back to x, or produce non-finite sample points.
Require both function evaluations to be finite numeric scalars. This exercise uses smooth functions.

hints.title: Sample symmetrically
hints.body: Two evaluations on opposite sides cancel the leading one-sided error.

hints.title: Check representability
hints.body: Floating-point numbers have finite spacing. An extremely small step may not move the sample at all.

hints.title: Read the discrepancy
hints.body: Try several h values. Truncation error grows with large steps; cancellation can dominate tiny ones.

explanation: Central differences approximate the tangent using a symmetric secant. For a smooth function, the leading truncation error is proportional to h².
A gradient check is a diagnostic, not a training algorithm: evaluating every parameter twice is expensive.
An inaccurate numerical derivative does not automatically prove the analytic gradient wrong. Check step size, precision, and whether the function is differentiable there.
